drafted_from: tool:find-when-a-character-speaks's row in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/ and the tests in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find when the parrot speaks in recording rec-a: score it with the seeds I labelled." It runs tool:find-when-a-character-speaks (step score) on your computer and writes the recording's turns file.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads one settings row of yours (record:setting:measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>) or the settings you pass, and works on files in the show's folder.
instructions: 1. Clone the repository https://github.com/Trillion-X/trillion-workshop and check the needs listed on the row (python 3 and its libraries, ffmpeg where named).

2. Your AI reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list and input {"tool":"tool:find-when-a-character-speaks"}, saves your settings row (records:read record:setting:measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>) to a file and puts it in the request as settings_record, or passes settings.

3. It runs: python3 -I trillion-workshop/tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/find_voice.py < REQUEST.json. First embed two or three recordings you know (step embed with audio and out), then label the character's stretches (step seed with npz, label and ranges "a-b,a-b") and some of other high voices under another label, then step score.

4. Check the precision and recall with do-work/check_seed_model.py and check_voice_finder.py before step batch over the catalog; show/show_turns.py prints each turn with its caption words to check by reading.

worked_examples.title: Score one recording after seeding
worked_examples.ask: Find when the parrot speaks in rec-a.
worked_examples.given: From VoiceFinderTest in tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/test/test_measures.py. The AI reads the row with tools:list, then runs in the show folder: python3 -I trillion-workshop/tools/measure-a-characters-voice-lines-and-staging/do-work/find_voice.py < REQUEST.json with REQUEST.json = {"step": "score", "data_folder": "show", "npz": "show/voice/rec-a.emb.npz", "json": "show/voice/rec-a.turns.json", "settings": {"character_label": "parrot", "embed_min_pitch_hz": 180.0, "embed_pitch_ratio": 1.4, "gate_pitch_ratio": 1.6, "gate_max_hz": 220.0, "voice_cosine_min": 0.5}}. rec-a.emb.npz holds the made-up windows (the parrot high, from 10 to 14 s and 30 to 33 s); the seeds hold parrot (16 windows) and guest (8 windows).
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"id": "rec-a", "duration_s": 41.0, "character_s": 7.0, "turns": 2, "json": "show/voice/rec-a.turns.json"}}; rec-a.turns.json lists the turns [[10.0, 14.0], [30.0, 33.0]] with gate_hz 176.0 (1.6 x the recording's median 110 Hz) and not the guest's 20-23 s.
